newsitem.title: USA: Diabetics at risk for many health problems.
newsitem.headline: Diabetics at risk for many health problems.

text.p: People over age 45 with diabetes are at risk for a host of medical problems, including heart disease and depression, once thought to be unrelated to diabetes itself, according to a study released on Wednesday.

Those complications added $4.1 billion to health care costs in the United States in 1991, according to the study by the Medical Technology and Practice Patterns Institute in Washington, which appeared in the journal of Clinical Endocrinolgy and Metabolism.

"Where we once thought blindness, amputations and kidney failure were the only conditions that could result from diabetes, now we must consider septicemia, or 'blood poisoning,' respiratory failure, depression and hip fractures as profound health threats that are linked to this disease too," said Dr. Terry Taylor, a co-author of the study.
Another co-author, Dr. Robert Ratner, said it was not clear whether diabetes increased the risk of developing these problems or whether it made the problems more severe in diabetics.
But the study concluded that diabetics ended up in the hospital more often, and longer, for a number of problems.
For instance, diabetics between age 45 and 64 have a five times greater chance of being hospitalized for liver disease than non-diabetics.
Diabetics over age 65 have a hospitalization rate for depression that is twice as high as their non-diabetic peers, the study said.
Diabetes affects about 16 million Americans. It cannot be cured but it can often be managed and treated.
